summary: Sequenced failover caused ordered-response gaps and customer escalations — TangentLogistics post-incident
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-11 at ~08:40 PDT multiple TangentLogistics production routes experienced an ordered-response gap after an automated sequenced failover. Customers observed partial or missing completion segments when using streaming chat endpoints; some requests returned 5xx responses during retries. TangentLogistics raised an urgent escalation to Support and SRE due to business-critical SLAs being impacted.

Impact:
- TangentLogistics (enterprise) saw ~18% of in-flight chat sessions return incomplete transcripts during the 18-minute window.
- Streaming clients experienced truncated or missing trailing tokens; a subset retried and generated duplicate completions causing downstream idempotency failures.
- Estimated customer request volume impacted: 12k requests; revenue-affecting for peak logistics dispatch.

Timeline (abridged):
- 2026-03-11 08:39 UTC: autoscaler triggered a rolling sequenced failover to shift load between GPU pools in us-west due to a noisy-neighbor detection.
- 2026-03-11 08:40–08:50 UTC: control-plane sequencer executed staged termination of worker shards; routing table updates propagated with partial acknowledgment.
- 2026-03-11 08:41–08:57 UTC: clients observed stream truncation and 5xx spikes; automatic client retries caused duplicate completions for some sessions.
- 2026-03-11 08:58 UTC: mitigation applied (temporary sequencer lock, forced fallback to stable pool) and customer-facing rate limiting adjusted.
- 2026-03-11 09:05 UTC: bulk recovery completed; monitoring confirmed normal streaming behavior by 09:20 UTC.

Root cause (summary):
A sequencing race between the autoscaler's staged failover workflow and the routing reconciliation process allowed a small window where worker shards were deregistered but the streaming multiplexer still forwarded client frames that could not be reassembled. The combination of in-flight KV cache mismatch and an optimistic retry policy on the client side produced truncated streams and duplicate completions.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate a staged failover by scheduling a sequenced drain of 25% of worker shards while simultaneously toggling routing table updates with artificially delayed acknowledgements.
2) Initiate long-lived streaming sessions with medium-length responses (1k–2k tokens) and enable client retry within 2s of stream errors.
3) Observe for truncated trailing tokens and duplicated completion entries when retries succeed against a different worker without consistent prefix acceptance.

Logs/alerts referenced:
- Cloudwatch alarm: streaming-error-rate-us-west-03 triggered at 2026-03-11 08:42 UTC.
- Router logs: router-prod-us-west-3 showing r.t.reconcile > 1.2s window; 503 spikes aligned.
- Runtime traces: missing finalize-token calls on worker-shard-47 between 08:40–08:45 UTC.

Customer impact note:
TangentLogistics opened an escalation and requested a post-incident call. Business impact primarily from incomplete dispatch messages and duplicate commands fed into downstream systems. We committed to a remediation plan and billing credit review.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis focused on autoscaler misconfiguration causing noisy-neighbor migration. Deeper traces showed sequencing window where routing delta applied before workers had finished prefix/KV cache flush. Reproducer confirmed that when clients retried quickly after a 5xx, subsequent successful completions were missing earlier tokens because the accepting worker had an empty prefix. Engineering reproduced locally with failover orchestrator and fixed a race in the sequencer handoff logic. Evidence: deterministic trace from runtime with correlation IDs (tangent-req-*) demonstrating missing finalize calls.
Additional finding: the client-side retry backoff was too aggressive for long-lived streaming sessions; recommended SDK change to exponential backoff for stream failures.
Postmortem draft will contain timeline with exact RPC traces and kernel-selection logs for affected shards.
resolution:
Applied temporary mitigation: 1) engaged sequencer lock to prevent concurrent route reconciliation during staged failovers; 2) forced fallback of TangentLogistics traffic to a pinned, stable GPU pool for 45 minutes; 3) flushed per-tenant KV cache for affected sessions and invalidated partial stream tokens; 4) pushed hotfix PR to runtime (PR 4521) to add an atomic handoff between sequencer and router reconciliation. Customer credit: offered one week of complimentary dedicated capacity and a billing credit to offset duplicate completions during the incident window.
Permanent fix merged and rolled out to prod by 2026-03-13 with a gradual canary and monitoring thresholds tightened. Verified with TangentLogistics during postmortem call on 2026-03-14.
follow_up_actions: Engineering: revert optimistic client-stream acceptance until sequencer handoff is atomic (owner: @Liam) — due 2026-03-20
SRE: add a routing reconciliation invariant check and an alert for orphaned streams > 30s (owner: @Maya) — due 2026-03-18
DX/SDK: implement exponential backoff for streaming retries in JS and Python SDKs (owner: @Kai) — due 2026-03-25
Support: notify all enterprise customers with streaming sessions about the change and recommended client-side backoff (owner: @Aisha) — due 2026-03-16
Finance: evaluate billing-credit calculation and apply credit to TangentLogistics invoice (owner: @Rohit) — due 2026-03-15
